Run and configure the clients

Desktop client

Download a package for your platform from Get the game on the home page and extract the complete archive. Keep the executable with its bundled libraries and music directory. From an extracted native package, run bin/lineclash on macOS or Linux, or bin/lineclash.exe on Windows. From a source build, run ./clients/gui/lineclash (clients/gui/lineclash.exe on Windows). Build instructions are on Source.

In the main menu, Public servers loads the official directory from https://lineclash.example.org/api/. Local network searches nearby servers directly over UDP and uses their LAN address. Saved servers contains your locally stored endpoints and offers Add, Edit and Remove controls. Use Saved servers for private hosts and ports. You can save or edit an endpoint while it is offline; account credentials are optional until connecting. Public entries cannot be renamed or removed from the directory by a client. Favourite a public endpoint to keep a local copy. The default game port is 31457. For a server on this computer, use localhost. Public-server joins use the selected central account. Private/offline connections can use local nicknames and passwords; those accounts belong to that server and are created when it allows registration.

Select a room, choose a team if wanted, and ready up. The room host controls rules, bots and starting the round. Leave the room to return to the lobby; disconnect before choosing another server. Use Quit in the main menu or close the window to stop the desktop client.

Desktop preferences and saved servers

Use Settings → Controls to change gameplay bindings and display preferences. Music and SFX controls set their respective volume and enabled state. The menu plays the title theme; during a round, Music Player provides track selection, pause, seek and shuffle. Track attribution is available in the player, About and the website Credits page.

Preferences and saved server entries are stored locally:

Platform Preferences Saved servers
macOS / Linux ~/.lineclash_settings ~/.lineclash_servers
Windows %APPDATA%\LineClash\settings %APPDATA%\LineClash\servers

Close the client before backing up or changing these files. Saved authentication hashes can grant account access: keep them private. To reset preferences, close the game and rename the settings file; the next launch uses defaults. Keep the original file if you want to restore your bindings later.

Connection problems

Check the server host and game port first; the HTTP status port is not a game endpoint. Unreachable usually requires checking that the server is running, its address is correct and the game port is reachable through the firewall. Wrong credentials requires the correct password for that server. Server full requires a free slot, while Protocol mismatch requires a compatible client/server version. Access-denied or banned accounts require assistance from that server's administrator.

During an active-game connection loss, automatic reconnect freezes local play while the server reserves your slot. Escape cancels recovery in the desktop client. An expired reservation, completed round or server restart requires reconnecting normally. See game basics.

Central LineClash accounts

Open Account in the main menu and sign in with your central email and password. The client immediately uses that identity for public servers; no profile selection or extra confirmation is needed. If you join a public server while signed out, sign-in continues directly into the selected server. Open Account again to see your username and email or sign out. Sign out before entering another account. The client remembers only the last successful identity.

Alternatively, choose Sign in with a PIN. The client displays an eight-digit PIN and https://lineclash.kladhest.se/account/pin/. Open that page on any computer or phone, enter the PIN, sign in with your username or email and password, then choose Approve client. Confirm that the PIN matches your own game window before approving. The game checks for approval automatically and continues using the same central account session as password login. The PIN expires after five minutes and can be redeemed once. Use username / password instead or Escape cancels the client’s wait; a late approval cannot sign it in. Use Get a new PIN after expiry or a failed request. PINs are temporary client approvals, not passwords or recovery codes, and are never sent to game servers.

Choose Create a new account in the client, enter a public username, private email, password and matching confirmation, then choose Create account. If the website requires email activation, the client asks you to check your inbox instead of signing in. Open the activation link, choose Verify email, then sign in normally in the client. Use Resend activation or https://lineclash.kladhest.se/account/verify/ if the email did not arrive. Links expire after 24 hours and can be used once. When activation is disabled, registration signs you in immediately and returns to the server browser or continues the pending server connection. Recovery codes are no longer issued or accepted. Registration starts inside the client; optional email confirmation uses the website. Username and email must each be unique; the website’s configured password minimum applies. Email is used for sign-in; older accounts without email can still use their username. Forgot password? opens https://lineclash.kladhest.se/account/recover/. When the operator has configured SMTP, enter your registered email to receive a single-use reset link that expires after 30 minutes. Choose and confirm a new password on the website, then sign in again in the client. If SMTP is not configured, the recovery page explains that recovery is disabled. Accounts without an email cannot use email recovery. New clients do not require browser approval codes. The desktop and experimental Amiga client send login credentials only to the official HTTPS API with certificate and hostname verification.

The client remembers one username and private email address: ~/.lineclash_accounts on macOS/Linux, %APPDATA%\LineClash\accounts on Windows and PROGDIR:LineClash.accounts on AmigaOS. Older saved-profile files are read for their first valid entry; the next successful sign-in replaces the file with one identity. Passwords are cleared after each request. Login sessions stay in memory, last up to twelve hours and can be reused across verified public servers; sign in again after restarting the client. Sign-out revokes that client session and does not interrupt games already joined.

Each game connection receives a fresh challenge. The client approves it over HTTPS using the signed-in account session, bound to the selected public server address and port. The game server polls its own request to obtain the verified identity. Neither a central password nor the reusable central session token travels over the unencrypted gameplay connection. Older clients can continue using browser-code approval on updated servers. The website stores a password hash. An email password reset invalidates earlier browser sessions, native sessions and pending approved connections; it does not disconnect games already joined. Requesting a reset alone does not change the password. A newer reset email replaces the previous link. The game server never receives the central password or a reusable central login token.

Central handles appear as @handle and have an immutable account ID. They are mapped separately on each server; an existing local account with a matching name is never claimed automatically. Each server keeps control of its own permissions, bans and local game records. No existing local statistics are automatically transferred to a central profile.

The Account button opens the sign-in form or your signed-in account. Private/LAN play still supports local accounts and does not require the central website. Older clients can keep using local accounts on updated servers. Central approval requires a verified, live public directory identity for the server. During a central-service outage, existing games continue and local-account play remains available; new central sign-ins are unavailable.

The game TCP stream remains unencrypted. Browser authentication and server verification use HTTPS; chat and gameplay can be observed or altered on an untrusted network. A reconnect token is restricted to a reserved slot on one server and expires with that short reconnect window; it is not a central account credential.

Native AmigaOS 3.x preview

The experimental native frontend targets a 68020 without an FPU, AmigaOS 3.x and a running bsdsocket.library TCP/IP stack. It opens a 640×256, sixteen-colour Intuition screen. Use arrows, Space, Z, C, Tab, number keys and the mouse. The Account screen uses the same single identity and direct HTTPS sign-in through AmiSSL. Account creation is available directly in the client; email password resets use the website when SMTP is configured. Public discovery uses AmiSSL certificate and hostname verification in a separate process. The initial native frontend has no music/SFX playback or modern gamepad integration. See the repository's Amiga guide for build and emulator checks.

Controls and accessibility

Default desktop controls

Action Key
Move left / right Left / Right, or A / D
Rotate clockwise Up, or W
Rotate counterclockwise Z
Soft drop Down, or S
Hard drop Space
Hold C or Shift
Chat Tab
Ready in room R
Pause F5, subject to room permissions
Target a player / use a special 1–8 using the displayed player IDs

Change gameplay bindings in Settings → Controls. The room host starts rounds from the room controls. Spectators can use arrows to switch the watched player.

Make the game easier to read

Press F2 to open or close Settings. Its Display tab includes window size, piece patterns and high contrast; Audio contains music and effects preferences. These preferences are saved locally.

  • F6 cycles 75%, 100%, 125% and 150% window sizes, bounded by the available display. You can also resize the window.
  • F7 toggles distinct piece markers, so piece types can be identified without relying on color alone.
  • F4 toggles higher-contrast text.

F2, F4, F6 and F7 are reserved for those options and cannot be assigned to gameplay actions. Website controls also have visible keyboard-focus outlines, and the background respects reduced-motion preferences.

Xbox and PlayStation controllers

The desktop client uses SDL's controller mappings for supported Xbox and PlayStation pads over USB or Bluetooth. Enable Controller input in Settings → Display. Support depends on the operating system, connection and SDL mapping for the specific model.

Xbox / PlayStation In-game action
D-pad left/right or left stick Move
D-pad down or left stick down Soft drop
A / Cross Rotate clockwise
B / Circle Rotate counterclockwise
X / Square or LB / L1 Hold
Y / Triangle or D-pad up Hard drop
Start / Options Pause, subject to room permissions

Movement repeats while held. A stick dead zone prevents slight drift from moving pieces. Pads may connect or disconnect while the game runs. Input is ignored when the game loses focus or a dialog is open. Controllers follow the configured gameplay key bindings; keyboard and mouse remain available for menus, chat and special targeting. Full controller-only menu navigation is not provided.
